subject: Re: Post-call: EU & APAC multilingual evals / recommended models + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: multilingual eval priorities + next steps

Hi Ana / Kenji —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Key priorities you shared: 
- EU languages: FR/DE/ES/IT — strong accuracy on product descriptions and returns flow.
- APAC pilot: JA/KO — tone preservation on localized customer-facing copy.
- Latency target: sub-220ms p50 for chat use case (regionally routed).
- Quality guardrails: minimize hallucination on policy-sensitive responses.

2) Proposed evaluation plan (what we’ll deliver):
- Short benchmark run across three model candidates (rw-instruct-7b, rw-llama-13b-q4, rw-serve-13b-mv) on your prompt set.
- Deliverable: PDF evaluation report + the prompt set we used (attached), plus a benchmark dashboard link.
- Focus metrics: accuracy/intent match, localization quality (native speaker spot-checks), token cost estimates, latency profile.

3) Next steps / asks for you:
- Please confirm the two sample flows you want prioritized (I noted: returns flow + product detail generation).
- Sign the attached NDA amendment (if any) — we can accept DocuSign link or your standard PO.
- If possible, share 50-100 anonymized examples per language for the spot-check (we’ll treat them as confidential).

I’ll run an initial eval this week and circle back with recommended model(s) + links to the detailed report.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: multilingual eval priorities + next steps

Ana —

Great, thanks. Answering your questions and outlining our early recommendations: 

1) Short answer on model tradeoffs (EU):
- rw-llama-13b-q4: strong localization fidelity on romance & germanic languages in our internal evals; good cost/perf when quantized (Q4). Recommended first pass.
- rw-instruct-7b: cheaper, lower latency; good for non-critical copy generation but we’ve seen some regressions on subtle morphological cases in DE/IT.
- rw-serve-13b-mv: best single-model accuracy in our benchmarks but higher cost; consider for critical flows if budget allows.

2) JA/KO tone preservation:
- We’ll use locale-aware prompt prefixes and explicit tone anchors (examples attached in prompt set).
- Recommend few-shot examples per locale rather than zero-shot for customer-facing copy.

3) Plan for this week
- I’ll run baseline benchmarks on the three candidates against your prompt set and return a PDF summary + dashboard link by Thursday EOD.
- Neha, can you run native-speaker spot-checks for FR/DE/ES/IT and drop notes in the shared Drive?
- Vivek, can you confirm whether we should enable prefix-KV caching for the EU routing policy to meet the 220ms p50 target?

Actions: Ana to send sample files; Marissa to run evals; Neha/Vivek to run spot-checks/infra confirmation.

Marissa

All —

Quick internal note (added Lauren to keep leadership looped):
- Ran the baseline evals this morning. Preliminary lean: rw-llama-13b-q4 hits the best EU localization/cost balance; rw-serve-13b-mv shows the highest accuracy but 1.8x token cost.
- We observed a small quality regression on DE compound-noun agreement for rw-instruct-7b in longer contexts — flagging for model/regression monitoring in Optimize.
- For JA we’ll include register examples and compute a per-sample register-coherency score (native-speaker heuristic).

Planned deliverables: PDF report + shared Drive folder with prompt sets and spot-check notes (link in metadata). I’ll share the dashboard link when it’s ready.

Neha / Vivek: please confirm by EOD whether we can enable prefix-KV caching for EU routing. If not, we’ll note a potential latency delta in the report.

Thanks —
Marissa
